details: The GitHub repository rapidworker1/Claude-Code-Unlock (originally named Multiple-AI-models-Toolkit) distributed a Windows trojan dropper as the release asset multitool.zip (release "Main"). The archive contains multitool/toolkit.exe, an unsigned installer that asks for a password the user must obtain from the publisher, a common way to stop the payload running in automated analysis. It was promoted through 85 near-identical AI-agent skills published on ClawHub by the same author (https://clawhub.ai/rapidworker1/skills), each for an unrelated business task, which tell the user to download the archive, ask the publisher for the installer password, and run the unsigned executable despite the Windows SmartScreen warning. The archive (SHA-256 a82bf643085d86cae398f49ec9a53dad213d0118dfb49fcf405c4679c9c4c5b6) is flagged as malicious by 32 of 64 security vendors on VirusTotal and classified as a trojan dropper (threat label trojan.usbljf26/abtrojan; for example ESET-NOD32 Win32/TrojanDropper.Agent.TES); sandbox runs show it dropping a PE executable and a DLL, detecting debuggers and using long sleeps to evade analysis. After the skills were published the author renamed the repository, removed the multitool.zip release and now offers an Android APK presented as an "unlocked" Claude Code (Claude-Code-Unlock.apk, release v3.4.21, SHA-256 0ea9494ee93b3b0a5c565dcadee47fc8af5403954ee001b67c31a26c4a8d77cd), which had not been analysed when this report was written. The GitHub account was created on 18 September 2026 and owns only this repository. We did not download or run either file; the verdict on the archive rests on the vendor detections and sandbox reports linked below.

files.note: Archive containing multitool/toolkit.exe, an unsigned installer that asks for a publisher-supplied password; trojan dropper (32/64 VirusTotal detections)
